interconnect_topology_options_ahb: Single-Manager AHB-Lite: one address decoder + one Subordinate-to-Manager multiplexor (Figure 1-1). The decoder generates HSELx; the multiplexor routes HRDATA/HRESP/HREADYOUT back to the Manager.
Multi-Manager AHB / multi-layer AHB: requires an interconnect component providing arbitration and routing. See Multi-layer AHB Technical Overview (ARM DVI 0045) for details.
interconnect_topology_options_apb: Single APB Manager (bridge) + multiple APB Subordinates (peripherals); the bridge generates per-peripheral PSELx by address decode.
Single Manager bus only; APB has no multi-Manager arbitration.
interconnect_rules_ahb: Decoder: monitors HADDR during the address phase and asserts the appropriate HSELx during the data phase. Minimum decode granularity = 1KB (Section 4.2).
Decoder: drives an HSELx per Subordinate; can also drive multiple HSELx to a single Subordinate (Multiple Subordinate select pattern, Section 4.2.2).
Multiplexor: routes HRDATA / HRESP / HREADYOUT / HEXOKAY from the selected Subordinate back to the Manager. Must retime the multiplexor control to the data phase (Section 4.2 Note).
Default Subordinate: required if memory map is incomplete; provides ERROR for NONSEQ/SEQ at undecoded addresses, zero-wait OKAY for IDLE/BUSY.
HREADY chain: multiplexor combines all Subordinate HREADYOUTs into the single HREADY broadcast (Figure 4-2).
No master-side waiting: AHB-Lite is single-Manager; HSEL+HREADY+HTRANS jointly indicate when a transfer is active.
Interface protection using parity (AHB5 optional): see Section 12.
Generic interconnect can offer AHB as an interface option alongside AXI and APB (Section 4.4).
interconnect_rules_apb: AHB-to-APB bridge: appears as an AHB Subordinate on the AHB side and as the APB Manager on the APB side. Performs rate-adaptation (often inserts wait states on AHB while completing the APB Access phase).
AXI-to-APB bridge: PSLVERR maps to RRESP/BRESP = SLVERR.
Per-PSELx address decode in the bridge; only one PSELx asserted per transfer.
Optional PSLVERR support per Subordinate; if not implemented, the bridge input is tied LOW.
fields.default_signal_values_when_omitted_ahb: See AHB Section 3.5 (Write strobes interoperability) — if a Manager does not implement HWSTRB, the Subordinate must treat HWSTRB as if all strobes are HIGH. For optional signals (HBURST=0 width, HPROT=0 width, HMASTER=0 width), the receiving side must apply the appropriate defaults.
fields.default_signal_values_when_omitted_apb: See APB Table 2-1 footnotes — if a Subordinate does not implement PSLVERR, the AHB-to-APB bridge ties the PSLVERR input LOW.

slave_classification_ahb.memory_slave_general: Subordinate that maps to an address region and handles all memory accesses.
slave_classification_ahb.peripheral_slave_via_apb_bridge: AHB-to-APB bridge presents a single AHB Subordinate that internally fans out to APB peripherals.

apb_peripheral_classification: Non-PSLVERR-supporting peripheral (PSLVERR input to bridge tied LOW)
Fixed-2-cycle peripheral (PREADY may be tied HIGH)
Variable-latency peripheral (drives PREADY=LOW during ACCESS to insert wait states)
fields.ahb_to_apb_bridge_role: Connects the high-performance AHB bus to lower-bandwidth APB peripherals. The bridge appears as an AHB Subordinate (on the AHB side) and the APB Manager (on the APB side). It typically inserts wait states on AHB while completing the multi-cycle APB transfer. AHB ERROR responses map from APB PSLVERR.
interface_categories_ahb: Manager interface (initiates transfers; drives HADDR + HBURST + HSIZE + HTRANS + HPROT + HWRITE + HMASTLOCK + HWDATA + HWSTRB + (HNONSEC/HEXCL/HMASTER if AHB5)).
Subordinate interface (responds to transfers; drives HRDATA + HREADYOUT + HRESP + HEXOKAY).
Decoder (generates HSELx based on HADDR; one centralized decoder per AHB bus).
Multiplexor (selects HRDATA + HRESP + HREADYOUT + HEXOKAY from the selected Subordinate).
interface_categories_apb: APB Manager (the bridge): drives PADDR + PWRITE + PSELx + PENABLE + PWDATA + PSTRB + PPROT.
APB Subordinate (peripheral): drives PRDATA + PREADY + PSLVERR.
fields.register_slice_insertion_rule_ahb: AHB does not have AXI's register-slice-anywhere property because of the strict 1-cycle address phase + HREADY chain. Register-slice insertion on AHB requires careful handling of the HREADY chain (typically through an AHB-to-AHB bridge or pipelined HREADY).
fields.register_slice_insertion_rule_apb: Not specified; APB is intentionally a low-cost two-phase bus and register-slice insertion is rare.
fields.ahb_to_axi_bridge_summary: AHB-Lite Subordinate to AXI Manager (rare direction): protocol mismatch — AHB has no AxLEN equivalent for SEQ-only bursts; bridge typically maps each AHB beat to a single-beat AXI transaction. The reverse direction (AXI Manager to AHB Subordinate) is more common and uses an AXI-to-AHB-Lite bridge.

evidence.quote: Figure 1-1 shows a single Manager AHB system design with the AHB Manager and three AHB Subordinates. The bus interconnect logic consists of one address decoder and a Subordinate-to-Manager multiplexor. The decoder monitors the address from the Manager during the address phase so that the appropriate Subordinate is selected during the data phase of a transfer. The multiplexor routes the corresponding Subordinate output data back to the Manager. AHB also supports multi-Manager designs by the use of an interconnect component that provides arbitration and routing signals from different Managers to the appropriate Subordinates.

A single Manager system only requires the use of a Decoder and Multiplexor. A multi-Manager system requires the use of an interconnect that provides arbitration and the routing of signals from different Managers to the appropriate Subordinates. The minimum address space that can be allocated to a single Subordinate is 1KB.

If a system design does not contain a completely filled memory map, then an additional default Subordinate must be implemented. If a NONSEQUENTIAL or SEQUENTIAL transfer is attempted to a nonexistent address location, then the default Subordinate provides an ERROR response. IDLE or BUSY transfers to nonexistent locations result in a zero wait state OKAY response.
Figure 4-2 shows the multiplexor interconnection structure required to implement a design with three Subordinates.
Generic interconnect products can offer AHB as an interface option, among others such as AMBA AXI or AMBA APB.

When bridging from AHB to APB: PSLVERR is mapped back to HRESP=ERROR for both reads and writes; this is achieved by mapping PSLVERR to the AHB signal HRESP[0]. When bridging from AXI to APB: an APB error is mapped back to RRESP/BRESP=SLVERR.

evidence.quote: APB peripherals are not required to support the PSLVERR pin. Where a peripheral does not include this pin then the appropriate input to the APB bridge is tied LOW.
